evidence: placeOrder: checks the customer and products exist, calls product.reserve(item.quantity), builds OrderLines and applies pricing.discountFor(...). This is business coordination.
cancelOrder: calls order.cancel() and puts stock back for each line. This is a business rule.
Persistence is reached only through the injected gateway methods (findById, findBySku, updateStock, save). The file has no storage code of its own.
Record mapping is handed off to RecordMapping (toProduct, toCustomer, toOrder, toOrderRecord).
The file contains no HTTP, request/response or framework code.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: OrderService is a Fowler-style service in the business (domain) layer. It coordinates use cases: it looks up customers, products and orders through injected gateways, applies domain behaviour and saves the results through those gateways. Everything it does is business work. It checks that records exist and raises BusinessError. It calls product.reserve() and order.cancel(), applies the discount from PricingPolicy, puts stock back when an order is cancelled, and totals the order lines with Money. It contains no persistence mechanics (no SQL, connections or storage formats), and the record-to-domain mapping is handed off to RecordMapping. It also has no transport or framework code (no HTTP, requests/responses or status codes). The cancelOrder restock adds to record.stock directly instead of going through a domain method. That is a small design-quality point, but it is still a business rule kept in the business layer. The imports from persistence concern dependency direction, which is out of scope for this rule.
